sections.heading: Evolution of Indian space programme; ISRO activities & achievements

blocks.text: India's space programme, begun by **Vikram Sarabhai**, is run by **ISRO (1969)** under the **Department of Space**. From the first satellite **Aryabhata (1975)** to **Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan**, ISRO is a globally respected, cost-effective space agency.

rows: **SLV, ASLV, PSLV (workhorse), GSLV, GSLV Mk-III/LVM3, SSLV**.
**Chandrayaan-1 (2008, found water), Chandrayaan-3 (2023, south-pole landing), Mangalyaan/MOM (2013, Mars in first attempt), Aditya-L1 (Sun)**.
**104 satellites in one PSLV launch (2017)**; low-cost missions.

sections.heading: 🚀 Exam-ready deep coverage: ISRO & the space programme

items: **Founded** by **Vikram Sarabhai (1969)**; DoS/ISRO HQ Bengaluru; first satellite **Aryabhata (1975)**; first launch vehicle **SLV-3 (1980, Rohini)**.

**Launch vehicles**: **PSLV** ('workhorse' — Sun-synchronous/polar orbits; the **104-satellite record, 2017**), **GSLV** (geostationary, cryogenic upper stage), **GSLV Mk-III/LVM3** (heavy-lift — Chandrayaan-3, Gaganyaan), **SSLV** (small satellites).

**Milestones**: **Chandrayaan-1 (2008 — found water on Moon)**, **Mangalyaan/MOM (2013 — Mars in first attempt, cheapest)**, **Chandrayaan-2 (2019)**, **Chandrayaan-3 (2023 — first soft-landing near the lunar south pole)**, **Aditya-L1 (2023 — Sun)**, upcoming **Gaganyaan (human spaceflight)** & NISAR.
**Applications**: communication, remote sensing, navigation, weather, disaster management, education, tele-medicine.

prelimsPointers: **ISRO founded 1969** (from INCOSPAR 1962); founder **Vikram Sarabhai**; under the **Department of Space**.
**Aryabhata (1975)** — India's first satellite.
**PSLV** is ISRO's reliable 'workhorse'; **GSLV Mk-III/LVM3** for heavy payloads.
**Chandrayaan-1 (2008)** discovered water on the Moon; **Chandrayaan-3 (2023)** — first to land near the **lunar south pole**.
**Mangalyaan (MOM, 2013)** — India reached **Mars in its first attempt** (first Asian nation).
**Aditya-L1** — India's first solar mission (L1 point).
ISRO set a record launching **104 satellites in one PSLV flight (2017)**.
ISRO founded by **Vikram Sarabhai (1969)**; first satellite **Aryabhata (1975)**.
**PSLV** = polar workhorse (104-sat record 2017); **LVM3/GSLV Mk-III** = heavy-lift.
**Chandrayaan-3 (2023)** = first soft-landing near lunar **south pole**; **Mangalyaan (2013)** = Mars, first attempt.
**Aditya-L1** = Sun mission; **Gaganyaan** = human spaceflight (upcoming).

glossary.definition: The Indian Space Research Organisation (1969), India's national space agency.
The Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle — ISRO's reliable 'workhorse' rocket.
India's 2023 mission that soft-landed near the Moon's south pole.

blocks.text: India operates major **application satellite systems** — the **INSAT/GSAT** (communication), **IRS** (remote sensing/earth observation) and **NavIC/IRNSS** (navigation) constellations — serving telecom, broadcasting, weather, resource mapping and positioning.

rows: **Communication & broadcasting**; among Asia-Pacific's largest comsat systems; also meteorology.
**Indian Remote Sensing** — earth observation, resource/agriculture/disaster mapping; among the world's largest.
**Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System** — 7 satellites; regional GPS-like positioning.

items: **Communication — INSAT/GSAT** series: telecom, TV broadcasting, weather, disaster warning, tele-education/medicine (geostationary).
**Remote sensing — IRS series** (one of the world's largest): resources, agriculture, forestry, urban planning, disaster mapping (polar/Sun-synchronous).
**Navigation — NavIC (IRNSS)**: India's regional navigation system (7 satellites), + **GAGAN** (GPS augmentation for aviation).
Applications feed agriculture (crop forecasting), fisheries (INCOIS PFZ), disaster response, telemedicine, e-governance.

prelimsPointers: **INSAT/GSAT** — communication & meteorology satellites (geostationary).
**IRS (Indian Remote Sensing)** — one of the largest earth-observation constellations.
**NavIC (IRNSS)** — India's regional navigation system; **7 satellites**; ~1500 km beyond borders.
Remote-sensing series — **Cartosat (mapping), Resourcesat, Oceansat, RISAT (radar)**.
**GSAT** series handles communication/broadcasting.
NavIC provides **Standard & Restricted** positioning services.
Applications — **weather, agriculture, disaster management, telecom, navigation**.
**INSAT/GSAT** = communication/weather (geostationary); **IRS** = remote sensing (polar).
**NavIC (IRNSS)** = India's regional GPS (7 satellites); **GAGAN** = GPS augmentation for aviation.
**Cartosat** = mapping; **RISAT** = radar imaging; **Oceansat/Scatsat** = ocean/weather.
Uses: crop forecasting, fisheries (PFZ), disaster mapping, tele-education.

glossary.definition: India's regional satellite navigation system of seven satellites.
The Indian Remote Sensing satellite series for earth observation.
India's communication and meteorological satellite systems.

blocks.text: Beyond civilian use, India operates **defence/military satellites** for secure communication and surveillance, and pioneered **educational satellites** — **EDUSAT (GSAT-3, 2004)**, the first Indian satellite dedicated entirely to education.

rows: Coordinates military space assets; **Mission Shakti (2019)** — ASAT test.

sections.heading: 🚀 Exam-ready deep coverage: defence & academic satellites

items: **Academic/education**: **EDUSAT (2004)** — India's first satellite dedicated to education (distance learning); GSAT-based tele-education.

**Defence/strategic**: **GSAT-7 'Rukmini' (Navy), GSAT-7A (Air Force)**; **RISAT & Cartosat** for surveillance; **Microsat/EMISAT** (electronic intelligence); **Mission Shakti (2019)** — anti-satellite (ASAT) test made India the **4th ASAT power**.
**Defence Space Agency (DSA)** & the private-sector opening via **IN-SPACe** and **NewSpace India Ltd (NSIL)** boost strategic & commercial space.
Student/academic small satellites (university-built) also launched by ISRO (e.g., APSAT / student satellites).

prelimsPointers: **EDUSAT (GSAT-3, 2004)** — India's **first satellite exclusively for education**.
**GSAT-7 'Rukmini'** — Navy; **GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird'** — Air Force communication.
**EMISAT** — electronic intelligence; **RISAT** — radar imaging (all-weather surveillance).
**Mission Shakti (2019)** — India's **anti-satellite (ASAT)** missile test (4th nation).
**Defence Space Agency (DSA)** coordinates military space assets.
Defence satellites provide **secure communication, surveillance, reconnaissance**.
**GSAT** = geostationary communication satellites.
**EDUSAT (2004)** = first education-dedicated satellite.
Defence sats: **GSAT-7 (Navy), GSAT-7A (Air Force)**; **RISAT/Cartosat** for surveillance.
**Mission Shakti (2019)** = ASAT test → India **4th** ASAT nation.

blocks.text: The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO, 1958)** is India's premier military-research body, developing **missiles, aircraft, radars, armaments and defence technologies** to make India self-reliant in defence.

rows: **Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag** (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme — A.P.J. Abdul Kalam).
Radars, EW systems, torpedoes, missile defence (BMD), **BrahMos** (India-Russia).

items: **DRDO (1958)** — premier defence R&D agency (Ministry of Defence); ~50 labs; mission = self-reliance (Atmanirbhar) in defence.

**Missiles — IGMDP (Kalam)**: **Prithvi (surface-surface), Agni (ballistic, Agni-V ICBM ~5000+ km, MIRV Agni-P), Akash (SAM), Nag (anti-tank), Trishul**; **BrahMos** (Indo-Russian supersonic cruise), **Astra** (air-air), hypersonic (HSTDV).
**Other systems**: **Tejas (LCA)**, **Arjun tank**, radars, EW, torpedoes, UAVs, **Pinaka** rocket, ballistic-missile defence, DRDO's role in **Covid** (ventilators, medicines).
**Strategic**: nuclear-capable delivery, **Agni-V**, submarine-launched (K-series), integrated with the nuclear triad.

prelimsPointers: **DRDO founded 1958**; under the **Ministry of Defence**.
**IGMDP** (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme) — **Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag**; led by **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**.
**Agni** — long-range ballistic missile series; **Prithvi** — surface-to-surface.
**Tejas (LCA)** — indigenous light combat aircraft.
**BrahMos** — supersonic cruise missile (India-Russia joint venture).
DRDO develops **radars, EW, torpedoes, ballistic-missile defence**.
Mission — **self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in defence**.
**DRDO (1958)** = defence R&D; ran **IGMDP** (Kalam): Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Nag, Trishul.
**Agni-V** = ICBM (~5000+ km); **BrahMos** = Indo-Russian supersonic cruise missile.
Platforms: **Tejas (LCA), Arjun tank, Pinaka, Astra**; hypersonic **HSTDV**.
Supports the **nuclear triad** (K-series SLBMs).
